deep.reconstruction:
Section B of a short study of the two special elliptic curves with extra automorphisms. Section A was presumably the 'square' Gaussian case, j=1728, Aut = mu_4. This section treats the 'hexagonal' case, j=0, Aut = mu_6.

(1) Claim. Consider elliptic curves over C with CM by Z[zeta], zeta = exp(2 i pi/3), taken with isomorphisms as morphisms. This groupoid is equivalent to the groupoid of oriented hexagons, i.e. torsors S under Z/6Z. Grothendieck identifies Z/6Z with mu_6(C), with the units of Q(cube root of 1) = Q(sqrt(-3)), and with the units of Z[zeta] = Z[T]/(1+T+T^2).

(2) Functor. Put El_1 = C/Z[zeta], the equianharmonic curve. For a torsor S set El_1(S) = El_1 wedge^{Z/6Z} S. This is the contracted product (El_1 x S)/(Z/6), where Z/6 = mu_6 acts on El_1 by complex multiplication. Since both groupoids are connected with automorphism group mu_6, the functor is an equivalence. Together with section A, this gives a combinatorial model of the residual gerbes B mu_6 (j=0) and B mu_4 (j=1728) of the moduli stack M_{1,1}.

(3) Intrinsic construction. Realize the combinatorial oriented hexagon S canonically as a regular hexagon in a Euclidean plane V_S, with origin at the barycenter of S. This is canonical up to similarity. Let Gamma_S be the lattice generated by the vertices; it is the hexagonal lattice. Set X_S = V_S/Gamma_S. The oriented conformal (Euclidean) structure of V_S gives X_S its complex structure, and X_S is canonically isomorphic to El_1(S).

The inverse functor is implicit. To E one attaches the set of the six shortest nonzero vectors of H_1(E,Z) for the flat metric, which is a mu_6-torsor. Note that the vertices of S lie in Gamma_S, so S is not a set of points of X_S. Rather, S is the set of minimal periods.

(4) The figure. It shows the regular hexagon with vertices labelled zeta, -zeta-bar, 1, zeta-bar, -zeta, i.e. the sixth roots of unity. Inside are an inscribed hexagram and circled dots. These are plausibly the triangle centres, i.e. the points (2+zeta)/3-type points with nontrivial stabilizer under the order-3 rotation; the identification is uncertain.

Purpose in the 1983 Teichmüller notes: to have rigid combinatorial base points and objects for the special points of M_{1,1}. These serve the 'Lego'/Teichmüller-tower and Galois-action programme later sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984).
errors: 'Q(cube root of 1)' is loose notation for Q(zeta_3) = Q(sqrt(-3)). 'Groupe des unités de Q(...)' must mean the units (equivalently, roots of unity) of the ring of integers Z[zeta]; Grothendieck corrects this himself on the next line.

The identification Z/6Z ≅ mu_6(C) is only valid over C, and the choice of orientation amounts to a choice of i. Over a non-closed field such as Q, the residual gerbe at j=0 is B mu_6, with twists classified by K*/K*^6 (y^2 = x^3 + a). Constant Z/6Z-torsors (oriented hexagons) would not give the Galois-correct picture. This matters if the construction is meant to be compatible with the Gal(Q-bar/Q) action.
Minor: the Euclidean structure is only canonical up to scaling, but only the oriented conformal class is needed for the complex structure, so this is harmless.

ideas.what: Groupoid of elliptic curves with j=0 (CM by Z[zeta_3]) equivalent to the groupoid of mu_6-torsors (oriented hexagons); twisting El_1 = C/Z[zeta] by a torsor via contracted product
ideas.modern_name: Residual gerbe B mu_6 of M_{1,1} at j=0; twisted forms / sextic twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Deligne–Rapoport, Deligne–Mumford stack theory; classical theory of twists via Galois cohomology)
ideas.where_published: The idea of special points with extra automorphisms of M_{1,1} as base points appears in spirit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this exact formulation is not known to me in published form

ideas.what: Canonical construction X_S = V_S/Gamma_S from the regular Euclidean realization of a combinatorial oriented hexagon, with complex structure from the oriented Euclidean structure
ideas.modern_name: Flat (equilateral) structure on the j=0 torus; hexagonal lattice; minimal-vector torsor in H_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; equilateral-triangulation viewpoint later in Shabat–Voevodsky (1989/1990)
ideas.where_published: Related equilateral-structure ideas in Esquisse d'un programme (dessins d'enfants, canonical Riemann surfaces from combinatorial maps)

ideas.what: Presentation Z[zeta] = Z[T]/(1+T+T^2); unit group = mu_6

missed.claim: This gives an explicit combinatorial (oriented-hexagon) model of the stacky point j=0 of M_{1,1}, intended as a rigid base object in the 1983 Teichmüller/Lego programme. It is a documented precursor of the Esquisse treatment of special points, but the mathematics is standard and the Galois-equivariant refinement (mu_6 versus Z/6Z) is not addressed on the page.
missed.quote: La catégorie de ces courbes équivalente à celle des hexagones orientés, i.e. des torseurs S sous Z/6Z ≃ mu_6(C)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest only: it shows how Grothendieck combinatorialized orbifold points of moduli stacks before Esquisse. It is not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean but routine description of the j=0 elliptic curve and its twists via mu_6-torsors, with a canonical Euclidean realization. Its value is historical, as a precursor to the Esquisse/Lego themes; there is no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Heading: 'Courbes ell. à multiplications complexes du type hexagonal' ('ell.' is an insertion above the line); the leading '3' is a section/page number.
The insertion near 'unités ... de Q(cube root of 1)' is illegible ('c.q.' / 'i.e.?'). The crossed-out line reads 'de Z[zeta] = Z[T]', rewritten as 'Z[zeta] = Z[T]/(1+T+T^2)'.
In 'El_1(zeta)', the argument is overwritten/struck and may originally have been a different symbol.

Figure: the vertex labels are zeta, -zeta-bar (top), 1 (right), zeta-bar, -zeta (bottom), i.e. the six sixth roots of unity. The interior contains an inscribed hexagram, and the circled dots are probably triangle centres rather than generic 'points du réseau'.

'réalise l'hexagone combin. S euclidiennement (canonique), dans [espace, struck] un plan euclidien V_S, origine choisie le barycentre de S'; the word replacing the struck one before 'engendré' is 'réseau'.
Last line: 'La structure euclidienne orientée de V_S définit la structure complexe de X_S' ('orientée' is underlined).
